comments.author: webdevatlurk
comments.story_title: Ask HN: What is your favourite tech talk?
comments.why_zh: 让评论者大开眼界的两个演讲之一
comments.quote_zh: 最早真正让我大开眼界的两个演讲是
comments.text_zh: 终于注册了账号来这个帖子里发言。我职业生涯还处于早期，主要做 Ruby、Python 和 JavaScript 相关的东西。你可能也猜得到，我看的主要是 Ruby、Python 和 JavaScript 相关的演讲。最早真正让我大开眼界的两个演讲是：- K Lars Lohn 在 2016 年 PyCon 上的主题演讲：[LINK] - Jim Weirich（RIP）在 RubyConf 2012 上的“Y Not”演讲：[VIDEO] 还有很多其他我很欣赏的演讲者：- Raymond Hettinger：他的演讲/教学风格是我希望自己效仿的；而且他是第一个讲如何写出正确的多线程/并发 Python 的人，那个演讲我能听懂并且用得上。- Brandon Rhoades：又一位演讲风格让我觉得很容易跟上的演讲者，另外他在 [LINK] 大约 18 分钟处还小小地调侃了一下 dd 工具）- Sandi Metz：我从 Python 世界起步，后来转到了 Ruby 世界，在那里接触到了 Sandi 的演讲。她讲的并不是极其复杂的话题，但她对一些非常基础的东西有很深的洞见，这对那些还见树不见林的新人很有帮助。- Robert Martin：据我所知，他的面向对象原则并非人人都推崇，但我觉得他的演讲很有用。- Gary Bernhardt：他的演讲在有趣和娱乐性方面是大多数演讲做不到的。名单还能继续列下去，但我现在没法全部想起来。
comments.text: Finally made an account to post in this thread. I'm rather early in my career doing mostly Ruby, Python and JavaScript things. As you might expect, I consume mainly Ruby, Python and JavaScript related talks. The first two talks that really blew my mind are: - K Lars Lohn's PyCon Keynote from 2016: [LINK] - Jim Weirich's (RIP) "Y Not" talk from RubyConf 2012: [VIDEO] There are many other presenters who I have a good opinion of: - Raymond Hettinger: his presentation/teaching style is something I'd like to model my own after, also he gave the first talk on writing proper threaded/concurrent python that I was able to understand and make use of. - Brandon Rhoades: another speaker with a presentation style that I've found easy to follow, also he takes a little shot at the dd utility about 18 minutes into [LINK] ) - Sandi Metz: I started out in Python land and moved to Ruby land, where I was introduced to Sandi's talks. She doesn't talk about incredibly complex topics, but she's got insight into some really basic things that's helpful to new people who can't see the forest through the trees. - Robert Martin: I gather that his OO principles are not universally revered, but I find his talks useful. - Gary Bernhardt: his talks are interesting and entertaining in ways that most are not The list goes on, but I can't think of them all right now.

comments.author: HCIdivision17
comments.story_title: Excitement Over Gravity Waves Comes Crashing Down
comments.why_zh: 通过 Y combinator 从 lambda 演算自举出计算
comments.quote_zh: 我最喜欢的视频之一——我还是没完全搞懂，但越来越接近了！
comments.text_zh: 我的意思是，没错，如果你想在不借助物理量（也就是带量纲的单位）的情况下定义宇宙，那确实会一路都是乌龟叠乌龟（无限递归下去）。我们目前还没有类似大统一理论的东西，能用某种基础数学来定义物理（就像我们通过 Y Combinator [0] 之类的东西，从 lambda 演算自举出计算那样）。再说，我们偶尔也会给无量纲量取带量纲的名字（我最喜欢的是工程单位“逆弧度”）[1]。这是个有用的抽象，对它抱怨似乎有点令人困惑。所以我们只能诉诸我们所知道的，也就是我们所看到的。我们看不到周围宇宙之外的东西，但我们可以试着从似乎行之有效的部分去外推。试图扼杀这种探索似乎有点……怎么说呢，毫无意义地对抗。这篇文章展示了科学在行动中的样子，做它最擅长的事：拿观察结果，通过理论与其他观察结果相协调，然后再修正理论使之匹配。我们的宇宙似乎遵循某些本身就是带量纲的方程，所以我不确定我们为什么不试着用宇宙自身来度量宇宙——我们也没有别的东西可用。即便是无量纲数也只有边际用处，比如 alpha；它可能“存在”并显现为我们的宇宙，但它并不特别具有预测性。[0] [VIDEO]（我最喜欢的视频之一——我还是没完全搞懂，但越来越接近了！）[1] [LINK]
comments.text: I mean, sure, it's going to be turtles the whole way down if you're looking to define the universe without resorting to physical quantities (that is, dimensioned units). We don't have anything like a Grand Unified Theory yet, wherein we define Physics by means of some elemental mathematics (in the form that we can bootstrap computation from lambda calculus via things like the Y Combinator [0]). Besides, we occasionally give dimensional names to dimensionless quantities (my favorite being the engineering unit the inverse radian) [1]. It's a useful abstraction, and it seems confusing to complain about it. So we resort to what we know, which is what we see. We can't see more than the surrounding universe, but we can try extrapolating from what seems to work. Attempting to stifle that inquiry seems a bit... I dunno, pointlessly antagonistic. This article shows science in action, doing what it does best: taking observations and reconciling them with other observations via theory, and then fixing theory to match. It seems our universe follows certain equations which are themselves dimensionful, so I'm not sure why we wouldn't attempt to benchmark the universe against itself - we don't have much else to use. Even dimensionless numbers are only marginally useful, like alpha; it may "exist" and manifest as our universe, but it's not especially predictive. [0] [VIDEO] (one of my favorite videos - I still don't grok it, but I'm getting closer!) [1] [LINK]

comments.story_title: An Interactive Guide to Ambiguous Grammar
comments.why_zh: 展示如何一步步从函数中抽离出自引用
comments.quote_zh: 一场慢慢扭曲并包裹一个语句、从而构建出 Y-combinator 的演讲
comments.text_zh: 读到这里，我猛然发现它让我想起一场演讲：那场演讲慢慢扭曲并包裹一个语句，从而构建出 Y-combinator。这个过程拿一个自引用函数，慢慢把“自我”从中抽离出来。老实说，我完全不确定把一个函数变成匿名函数是否真的类似于把一个句子变成被动语态，但也许现在重看那个视频，我会拥有那种难以言喻的“妙处”，让我真正搞懂这个过程。[0] [VIDEO]
comments.text: Reading this, I was struck by how it reminded me of a talk that slowly warped and wrapped a statement to build up the Y-combinator. The process takes a self-referential function and slowly works the self out of it. Honestly, I'm not at all sure turning a function anonymous is actually similar to making a sentence passive, but maybe re-watching that video now I'll have that je ne sais quoi that'll let me actually grok the process. [0] [VIDEO]
